_about: Lane C. ReachTEL final pre-election polls. 2016 final fully captured: the complete 7 News national release of 30 June 2016 (Q1-Q8) re-fetched from Wayback (capture 20190313050557) after IA recovered late in the pass. 2019: NO final ReachTEL federal poll exists — ReachTEL's federal series (then Sky News/Equifax-era) stopped appearing in the polling record after 6 Aug 2018.

waves.finding: ReachTEL '7 News - National Poll - 30 June 2016' (reachtel.com.au ReachtelBlog; published 1 Jul 2016)
waves.method: automated telephone survey system; numbers and persons within household selected at random; results weighted by gender and age to ABS figures; conducted during the evening of 30 June 2016
fragments: Headline column is the LEANED one (printed '30th June*': Liberals 38.9% + Nationals 3.9% = L-NP 42.8, Labor 34.6, Greens 10.7, NXT 1.5, Other 10.5 — sum 100.1; ReachTEL prints its own caveat 'due to rounding, not all tables necessarily total 100%'). The UNLEANED 30 June column: Liberal 37.6, Nationals 3.9, Labor 33.3, Greens 10.3, NXT 1.4, Other 8.5, Undecided 5.1 ('Undecided voters were asked a follow-up question on who they would have even a slight leaning towards').
2PP trend table (respondent-allocated, printed): 26 May 48/52, 2 Jun 50/50, 9 Jun 50/50, 16 Jun 51/49, 23 Jun 51/49, 30 Jun 51/49 (Liberal-National cf. Labor).

Q2 Better Prime Minister, 30 Jun (with demographic splits printed): Turnbull 52.9 / Shorten 47.1; by party — L/NP 95.2/4.8, Labor 10.4/89.6, Greens 23.7/76.3, Und 51.9/48.1; Female 50.4/49.6, Male 55.4/44.6.
Q3/Q4 performance ratings printed with party splits (Turnbull very-good+good 31.2 cf. poor+very-poor 36.9; Shorten 34.8 cf. 38.6) — matches the PB relay.

Q5 expected outcome by AGE (printed): Coalition win — 18-34: 50.6, 35-50: 53.8, 51-65: 56.4, 65+: 60.1; Labor win — 29.4, 26.0, 14.9, 14.4; Hung parliament — 20.0, 20.2, 28.6, 25.5. (Expectations, not VI.)
waves.note: Q1 carries no demographic splits (trend waves + leaned column only); the page's gender/age crossbreaks sit on Q2 (PPM) and Q5-Q8 (expectations, campaigning, Brexit, issues) — none are voting intention, so dims is empty and the breaks live in fragments. No state splits printed anywhere in the release. PB relay (1 Jul 2016) confirms the topline and adds that the previous-election preference basis 'would produce the same result' 51-49; Wikipedia's tabulated row gives Others 12 (= NXT 1.5 + Other 10.5).

sources.note: the complete 30 Jun 2016 release (Q1-Q8 with crossbreaks) — Wayback capture re-fetched when IA recovered
PB final-roundup corroboration of the ReachTEL topline

notes: 2019-05-18 election: NO ReachTEL wave exists to file. Evidence: (1) Wikipedia's 2019-cycle polling table's last ReachTEL federal row is 6 Aug 2018 (src/newspoll/wikipedia-opinion-polling-2019-wikitext.txt, ReachTEL rows chronological 2017→2018-08); (2) Poll Bludger's complete post list for the final 2019 campaign week (10-19 May, 21 posts) contains no ReachTEL national poll; (3) the 7 News/Sky News ReachTEL series itself ended in this era — the 2017 capture's own blog archive (saved in 2016-final-7news-30june16-body.txt) shows the blog petering out after May 2017, consistent with the house's sale to Equifax/illion and exit from published federal polling. Filed as a pollster-level absence, not a fetch failure.
ReachTEL 2016 headline VI primaries are the 'forced preference'/leaned basis; the unleaned column is preserved verbatim in fragments (undecided 5.1% rides und on the wave).
gaps: 2016-07-02: state-level VI splits — never printed in the 7 News release (confirmed from the full body this pass). Nothing left to find for 2016.

2019-05-18: no poll exists (see notes) — nothing more to find.
